official.description: The Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund was set up in memory of Sonja Davies, a renowned women's rights campaigner, social activist, trade union leader and politician, and promotes initiatives that advance peace in New Zealand. It is available to a woman or a group led by a woman who is developing an initiative that will help create a more peaceful world at home, school, the workplace or in the community, including work on the elimination of family violence, understanding and cooperation between groups, and mediation or conflict resolution.

applicant_utility.summary: The Sonja Davies Peace Award Fund pays up to NZD 4,000 to a woman, or a woman-led group, to carry out a peace-building initiative in New Zealand, and the Trust opens the form for only 19 days: 12 to 30 October 2026. The money follows a costed project plan rather than a course enrolment, so the strength of the initiative and the applicant's track record in delivering it matter far more than any academic transcript. One of the three eligible categories is an individual enrolled at a tertiary institution, but this is a project grant rather than a course scholarship. Anyone who has previously received any New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award is barred outright.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A woman, or a woman-led group, with a costed peace-building project already taking shape - family-violence prevention, intergroup understanding, mediation or conflict resolution - and a demonstrated record of delivering that kind of work.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the applicant team's history before drafting: a previous award from any Hine Kahukura fund disqualifies the applicant entirely
Draft the project timeline and budget first, because two of the three things the panel weighs are the budget and the timeline
Frame the initiative description around how it will advance peace in New Zealand, rather than around the organisation's general mission
For group applications, name the woman project leader explicitly and keep evidence of her role and the group's stated aims
Assemble citizenship or resident-class-visa evidence plus proof of current New Zealand residence
Prepare the full application in September so it can be submitted in the first days of the window
common_rejection_risks: A previous Hine Kahukura award in the applicant's history, which is an automatic bar that groups often overlook when a former recipient is named as project leader
A budget that does not actually show how the $4,000 will be spent, or costs that the timeline does not support
Describing intent rather than capability - the panel weighs experience of and demonstrated capability to conduct the initiative
Group applications where the woman project leader's role, or the group's peace-promotion aims, are never documented
Submitting after 30 October, since the Trust does not accept late applications
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any cost of the initiative above $4,000, plus organisational overhead not itemised in the budget. This is not a stipend: it does not cover tuition, living costs or travel, and the maximum is $4,000 rather than a guaranteed amount.
document_audit: The Trust publishes only the timeline and budget as supporting material for this fund, so keep the budget legible, itemised and matched line-by-line to the initiative description
Informal-group applicants need evidence that peace promotion is among the group's stated aims
Residency evidence must show both status (citizen or resident class visa) and current residence in New Zealand
Submission is confirmed by a message in the browser plus a confirmation email - check junk mail, and email the Trust if no confirmation arrives
alerts: The window is 12 to 30 October 2026 only - under three weeks - and the form is not live before 12 October
The published value is a maximum of $4,000, so budget and pitch for a realistic partial amount
Recipients of any New Horizons for Women: Hine Kahukura award are ineligible, including through the Education, Research and Personal Growth funds
The Trust does not provide feedback on applications, so there is no debrief to learn from
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete the Trust's online application form sometime between 12 and 30 October 2026 with the initiative description, timeline and budget; the Trust notifies outcomes by email.

applicant_utility.summary: The Toloa Tertiary Scholarship gives Pacific students in their second year or beyond of a full-time STEM degree up to NZD 10,000 for one year, paid straight to the institution against its invoice, so it works like a fees offset rather than cash in hand. Only ten tertiary scholarships are on offer each year against 400 secondary ones, and the tertiary window is short: the 2026 round opened on 18 November 2025 and closed at 5pm on 9 February 2026. The hard eligibility gate is year of study - first-year students are excluded, and so are students in their final year or Year 3 because the Government fees-free programme already covers them. Start early, because the application needs an enrolment record, a prior-year academic transcript, an institutional invoice and documented Pacific Indigenous descent.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A Pacific student who has finished their first year, is locked into full-time STEM study, and is not yet in the final year or Year 3 of the programme.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm the year-of-study gate first: not first year, and not final year or Year 3 of a STEM programme
Request an invoice from the tertiary institution early, since funds are paid against it and it is submitted with the application
Locate your National Student Number through the NZQA website before starting the form
Pull the prior academic year's records, which must be supplied with the application
Gather descent evidence now - passport or birth certificate, or a parent's or grandparent's Pacific Island documents; if none exist, request the community leader endorsement well before the deadline
List every scholarship awarded or pending for the year, as the application requires a full declaration
common_rejection_risks: Applying in the first year of tertiary study, which is not eligible
Being in the final year or Year 3 of a STEM programme, where the Government fees-free programme applies instead
A programme outside STEM - social sciences and frontline healthcare qualifications are explicitly not funded
An incomplete application, because only applications completed correctly are reviewed
Descent evidence that does not link to the applicant, or is left to be chased after the deadline
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Any fee above the awarded amount and general living costs: the $10,000 is a cap paid to the institution against its invoice rather than to the student, and travel (local, national and international) is explicitly excluded except for PhD research or fieldwork costs. Wages, debt repayment and capital spending are also excluded.
document_audit: The institutional invoice is not optional - it is what the payment is calculated against, so obtain it before the window opens
Descent evidence may be a parent's or grandparent's Pacific Island passport or birth certificate showing village and birthplace, as long as the surname links to the applicant
If no family documents exist, Le Va publishes an endorsement form for a community leader, which needs lead time to obtain
The form can be saved and returned to once the eligibility section is approved, so gather documents while the eligibility step is assessed
The National Student Number is available from NZQA or the institution if you cannot find it
alerts: The scheme runs annually: the 2026 tertiary round closed at 5pm on Monday 9 February 2026, with applications opening in mid-November, so watch the Le Va page from November
Only ten tertiary scholarships are awarded each year, against 400 secondary scholarships
Notify Le Va at toloa@leva.co.nz if you change programme or papers, because a STEM-related programme must remain full-time to stay eligible
Travel costs are not funded, other than research or fieldwork expenses for PhD students
Repeat applications are allowed - a past recipient can apply again
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Complete Le Va's online Toloa form once the round opens, clearing the eligibility section, then submit with enrolment proof, prior-year records, the institutional invoice and descent evidence; the award is paid directly to the tertiary institution.
